newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas retreats ahead of milder weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas retreats ahead of milder weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices retreated from midweek highs on Thursday as milder temperatures were forecast for most of the U.S. by this weekend, industry sources said.

Louisiana Gulf Coast prices at the Henry Hub erased Wednesday's gains by falling about 11 cents to $2.10-2.11 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), converging for the most part with current May values. Transco was quoted equally lower at $2.12-2.17.
Similarly in south Texas, where temperatures are also moderating, prices tumbled 13 cents to the low-$2 area.
At 1337 EDT, May Henry Hub natgas futures were up two cents at $2.08 before expiration later today.

In the Northeast, spring-like weather pushed New York city-gate prices at least 10 cents lower to about $2.35-2.40. Appalachian prices were down an equal amount to $2.30-2.32 on Columbia and the mid-to-high $2.30s on CNG.
At the Chicago city-gate, values fell an average of 20 cents to about $2.15.
Elsewhere in the Midcontinent, prices on average lost 11 cents to $1.93-1.96, with Demarcation quoted mostly in the low-to-mid $1.90s.
For the first-of-the-month, Midcontinent prices were talked in the low-to-mid $1.90s, indicating a gain of about 20 cents from April.

Further west, Permian basin prices slid about 20 cents to a wide range of $1.80-1.95, with the lower-priced deals evident in late morning trade. For May 1 delivery, market sources said gas was selling in the low-to-mid $1.90s, up about 30 cents from April indices.

Waha values for Friday were similarly weaker at $1.90-2.00, while southern California border prices fell to about $2.02-2.08. May gas at the border was quoted in the low-$2 area, up at least 25 cents from April 1.
Market sources attributed the bidweek strength to storage injection demand and an expected rise in air-conditioning demand.

American Gas Association said Wednesday that U.S. gas inventories were down seven bcf last week to 26 percent of capacity. Overall stocks are still 256 bcf, or 45 percent, above year-ago levels, with eastern storage 175 bcf over a year ago, almost double 1996 levels.
